Subject: FinchPay evaluation MAP & contracting stakeholders

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I wanted to kick off a short mutual action plan (MAP) so everyone has clear roles and milestones toward production evaluation and contracting. I’ve attached a first-pass MAP and a lightweight SOW draft for review.

Quick summary of proposed roles (please confirm or update):
- FinchPay procurement owner: Carlos Mendes (procurement/legal lead)
- FinchPay legal: Rachel Tan (contract review, redlines)
- Redwood commercial: Marissa Cole (deal lead)
- Redwood legal/ops: Priyom Das (contract shepherd)
- Redwood solutions: Laura Bennett (technical validation & runbook)

High-level milestones I propose:
1) MAP acceptance + deliverables list — 3 business days
2) Security questionnaire & checklist review — 5 business days
3) SOW redline cycle — 7 business days
4) Final contract and signatures (DocuSign) — target by 2026-05-28

Attachments: FinchPay_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with dates), RWI_SOW_draft_v0.3.docx, Vendor_Security_Checklist.pdf

Ask: Could Carlos and Rachel confirm the procurement and legal owners + your preferred redline process (DocuSign/Word redlines/Confluence)? Also please flag any hard constraints on the target signature date.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the MAP in HubSpot and keep the one-page tracker updated.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Marissa — thanks for the clear MAP and the materials. Confirming I’m FinchPay’s procurement owner for this engagement. A couple of notes from our side: 

1) Timeline: the target signature date of 2026-05-28 is aggressive but doable if we keep the redline window tight. We have a board commitment for a vendor going live in June, so we need contract execution before month-end.
2) Redline process: our legal prefers a Word redline returned to us for the initial pass, then a short finalization call if needed. We use DocuSign for signature execution but do not use it for negotiating changes.
3) Security review: our InfoSec team will complete the Vendor Security Checklist. They may request a short call with Laura for architecture Q&A.

I attached a scan of the procurement intake form (not included in this thread) — procurement won’t be able to consume the SOW until legal signs off on key terms (data residency, indemnity cap, termination for convenience).

I can commit to reviewing the first SOW redline by Friday (2026-05-15) if Priyom can get us the legal-ready draft by EOD Thursday.

—Carlos
Carlos Mendes
Head of Procurement | FinchPay
carlos.mendes@finchpay.com | +44 20 7946 0011

Hi Carlos — appreciate the quick confirmation and the constraints. That timeline works as long as we adhere to the proposed review windows. Plan: 
- Priyom will push a legal-ready SOW to you by EOD Thursday (2026-05-14).
- Laura will schedule a 30-minute technical sync with your InfoSec team for Friday (2026-05-15) to go over the checklist items.
- I’ll update the MAP with the fixed dates and push it into HubSpot so everyone has a single source of truth.

If anything slips we should flag it and decide whether to extend the signature target by a week or keep scope of the initial deployment limited.

Marissa

Hi all — looping in from Redwood legal/ops. Thanks, Carlos, for the procurement signal and the process preference. A few operational details from our side: 

- SOW redline: we’ll send the SOW as a Word doc with tracked changes. Please return a single consolidated redline PDF/Word file with comments; that helps us ingest edits quickly.
- Key terms we anticipate will be negotiated: data residency (we currently host in eu-west-1), liability cap (we typically propose 3x fees, happy to discuss), confidentiality/data handling annex, and termination clauses.
- We will not accept gating language that requires on-prem deployment for evaluation — if InfoSec needs further assurances we can provide a short-term SOC2 extract and an architecture call with Laura.
- Requested: could Rachel and/or Carlos point me to any internal clause templates (e.g., standard indemnity language) so we can map and limit redline churn?

We’ll target sending the legal-ready SOW by 2026-05-14 18:00Z. After your redline, let’s aim for a maximum 48-hour turnaround on Redwood’s side for counter-redlines to keep within the May target.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
